# Contract formation

## Elements of a contract

A valid contract requires an offer, acceptance, consideration and an intention to create legal relations. An offer is a clear statement of the terms on which one party is willing to be bound. Acceptance must match the terms of the offer, and a reply that changes the terms is a counter-offer. Consideration is something of value that each party gives or promises to give.

## Limits

A contract made by a person who lacks capacity, such as a young child, may not be enforceable. Silence does not normally count as acceptance. A party may withdraw an offer at any time before it is accepted. Agreements made as a social arrangement between friends usually lack an intention to create legal relations.
